newsitem.title: USA: White House says U.S. diplomat will leave Belarus.
newsitem.headline: White House says U.S. diplomat will leave Belarus.

text.p: The White House said on Sunday a U.S. diplomat would comply with the request of the government of Belarus that he leave that country after he was detained at the scene of an anti-government protest.
"He has been released, and the Belarus authorities have requested him to depart within 24 hours, and we of course will comply with that wish," a White House official said.

Earlier Belarussian state television said the diplomat, the U.S. embassy's first secretary Serzh Alexandrov, had been declared persona non grata and had been asked to leave the former Soviet republic.
A news anchorman read out a Foreign Ministry statement saying Alexandrov, an ethnic Belarussian, had taken part in actions "incompatible with his diplomatic status."

The White House official declined to comment on the circumstances under which the diplomat was arrested, but said: "We are extremely disturbed at the continuing slide toward authoritarianism in Belarus."

The Belarus Foreign Ministry statement said Alexandrov had been detained for "provocative actions" during violent clashes on Sunday between riot police and nationalist demonstrators protesting against the pro-Moscow policies of hardline President Alexander Lukashenko. About 70 other people were arrested.
The United States has been one of Lukashenko's strongest critics.

The official spokeswoman for the U.S. embassy in Minsk, Janet Demery, told Reuters that Western diplomats often watched Belarus protests from the sidelines "as part of a brief to observe the political situation but not to participate."
